name: 336. OpenAI-compatible chat sends price-affecting fields as sent or refuses them, and the encrypted-reasoning retry has a switch (compatible chat fields)
description: Local fixture regression for TXE-6527 (Bifrost–Tokun contract C3, C4 and C6), no live provider calls. Start tests/e2e/api/runners/provider-error-fixture.mjs, start an isolated gateway on tests/e2e/api/provider_config/provider-error-fixture.config.json (moonshot and deepseek base_url -> the fixture's /pp/oc, which records every request body; the harness's default setup token), and run with providerErrorFixture=1; every case is skipped otherwise. 336.2 and 336.3 send max_completion_tokens 5 and read the body the vendor received: moonshot gets max_completion_tokens 5 with prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_options.ttl, deepseek gets max_tokens 5. 336.4 and 336.6 send a service_tier outside the tier list of the fixture's oc-tiered capability record, non-streamed and streamed: 400 caller_unsupported_parameter naming service_tier, with no request at the fixture; 336.5 sends a listed tier with max_completion_tokens 5 and the vendor receives both. The gateway config sets no compat option, so 336.4 to 336.6 run with the compat plugin's parameter drop on (its default) against a model that has a capability record: the plugin drops neither field (TXE-7026). 336.7 is Azure OpenAI's documented blocked-prompt answer: the 400 and its content_filter code are kept and error_type is caller_content_filtered. 336.8 replays a reasoning item whose id does not match its encrypted token with the switch at its default: the fixture refuses it once and the stripped second call succeeds, two upstream calls. 336.9 to 336.11 read the client config, save it back with disable_encrypted_reasoning_retry on (the full object, as the dashboard saves it) and replay again: the vendor's 400 comes back after exactly one upstream call. 336.12 turns the switch back off; if a case between 336.10 and 336.12 stops the run, restart the fixture gateway. 336.9 to 336.12 share h336ClientConfig and must run in order. Red before the change: the vendor received max_completion_tokens 16 and no prompt-cache field, the unsupported tier was dropped and the request answered 200, the Azure error carried no content-filter class, and no switch existed.

item.name: 336.1 fixture counters and recorded requests reset
336.2 moonshot kimi chat reaches the vendor with max_completion_tokens 5 and both prompt-cache fields (compatible chat fields)

exec: pm.test('the request succeeded', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.equal(200); });
pm.test('the fixture reports what reached it', function () { pm.expect(err, String(err)).to.equal(null); pm.expect(res.code).to.equal(200); });
var calls = res.json().data[0].calls.filter(function (c) { return c.path === '/pp/oc/v1/chat/completions' && JSON.parse(c.body).model === 'oc-plain'; });
pm.test('one request reached the vendor', function () { pm.expect(calls.length, res.text()).to.equal(1); });
pm.test('max_completion_tokens is the 5 the caller sent, not 16', function () { pm.expect(sent.max_completion_tokens, calls[0].body).to.equal(5); });
pm.test('prompt_cache_key reached the vendor', function () { pm.expect(sent.prompt_cache_key, calls[0].body).to.equal('tenant-42'); });
pm.test('prompt_cache_options.ttl reached the vendor', function () { pm.expect(sent.prompt_cache_options && sent.prompt_cache_options.ttl, calls[0].body).to.equal('1h'); });
